partners.mechanism_chain: SOD1 variant —DISRUPTS→ SOD1 (HGNC:11001); SOD1 (HGNC:11001) —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 1 (MONDO:0007103); TALDO1 variant —DISRUPTS→ TALDO1 (HGNC:11322); TALDO1 (HGNC:11322) —DISRUPTS→ Pentose Phosphate Pathway (KEGG:00040); Pentose Phosphate Pathway (KEGG:00040) —DECREASES→ NADPH (CHEBI:15378); Pentose Phosphate Pathway (KEGG:00040) —DECREASES→ Ribulose-5-phosphate (CHEBI:17030); TALDO1 (HGNC:11322) —LEADS_TO→ Transaldolase deficiency (MONDO:0011624); NADPH (CHEBI:15378) —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 1 (MONDO:0007103); Ribulose-5-phosphate (CHEBI:17030) —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 1 (MONDO:0007103). Mutations in SOD1 (ALS1) and TALDO1 (transaldolase deficiency) can both lead to downstream cellular dysfunction. While SOD1 is primarily known for its role in oxidative stress response, its dysfunction can indirectly impact cellular redox balance and energy metabolism. TALDO1 is a key enzyme in the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), which is crucial for producing NADPH (for redox balance and biosynthesis) and pentose phosphates (for nucleotide synthesis). Loss-of-function in TALDO1 directly impairs PPP function, leading to reduced NADPH and altered nucleotide precursors. The convergence occurs because both impaired oxidative stress response (from SOD1 dysfunction) and impaired NADPH production (from TALDO1 dysfunction) can exacerbate cellular vulnerability to oxidative damage and compromise essential biosynthetic pathways, ultimately contributing to neurodegeneration seen in ALS and potentially other cellular deficits in transaldolase deficiency.
